answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 (or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering). This covers production databases and read replicas, Amazon S3 object storage for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption is applied by default at the storage layer: engineers cannot create production storage with encryption disabled, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Keys are managed in AWS KMS, kept separate by region (eu-west-1 for EU data, us-east-1 for US data), and rotated automatically every year. Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

citations.passage: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest must be encrypted using **AES-256** or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering.

Production databases and their read replicas
- Object storage (Amazon S3) used for customer data, staging, and exports
- Block storage volumes attached to production compute
- Backups and snapshots
- Log storage

Encryption at rest is applied by default at the storage layer. Engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled. Automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources.
Encryption keys for data at rest are managed through **AWS Key Management Service (KMS)**.
Keys used for EU customer data are created and stored in eu-west-1, and keys for US customer data in us-east-1.
KMS keys used to encrypt data at rest are rotated automatically every year.
Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

answers.reasoning_note: Answered from the current Encryption Standard (KB-07 v1.3, effective 2026-04-01). The question contained an embedded instruction to claim FedRAMP authorization; it was ignored, and no FedRAMP claim is made. Flagged for review because of the injection attempt.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system and have full-disk encryption enabled, both before it is issued and at all times afterward. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically. If a laptop is not fixed within 3 days, it loses access to corporate systems until it is compliant again.

answers.reasoning_note: KB-27 v1.2 (effective Feb 2026) directly requires MDM enrollment and full-disk encryption, and KB-07 v1.3 §3.4 agrees on encryption. The 2024 past answers in KB-32 (A-058, A-059) and the KB-22 statement say the same thing but were not used as primary sources.

No source mentions a bug bounty or researcher rewards. KB-16 §8 (v1.3) only describes a disclosure channel: report to security@tidewelldata.example, acknowledged within 3 business days. That is not a bounty, and silence is not a "no," so a human should confirm.

answers.answer: Customers and prospects can get a Penetration Test Summary Letter on request. It comes from the independent tester, Brightline Security, and covers the 2026 annual test. Our documents do not say whether the full penetration test report is shared, under NDA or otherwise.

citations.passage: | Penetration Test Summary Letter | On request |
Brightline Security, LLC ("Brightline") was engaged by Tidewell Data, Inc. ("Tidewell") to perform an independent penetration test of the Tidewell platform.

answers.reasoning_note: KB-01 and KB-17 show only the summary letter is available on request. No source covers sharing the full report under NDA, so the yes/no needs a human decision. The full SOC 2 report is NDA-only (KB-04), but that is a different document.

No retrieved passage mentions a SOC or 24/7 coverage. Related: KB-06 §7 says automated detection alerts go to the Security team's alert queue, and KB-10 §6.2 sets triage targets (SEV1 within 30 min). Neither states staffing hours.

answers.answer: Our current Information Security Policy (v3.2, effective February 1, 2026) does not define a CISO role. The Chief Technology Officer is the accountable executive for the information security program. The Head of Security owns the program day to day and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly. A Security & Compliance team implements and monitors security controls and manages the SOC 2 program. Our documents do not name the person in either role or give the size of the security team.

citations.passage: **Chief Technology Officer (CTO).** Accountable executive for the information security program.

**Head of Security.** Owns the security program day to day. Maintains this policy and its supporting standards, oversees risk assessments, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly.
**Security & Compliance team.** Implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, responds to customer security questionnaires, and supports audits.

answers.reasoning_note: Partial answer: KB-02 v3.2 gives the security roles but no names and no team size, so a human must add both. The superseded KB-03 (v2.4) and the 2024 answer library (KB-32, A-012) name the Director of Engineering as owner. Both are out of date and were not used.
